answer: Weight only accrues when attestations arrive from several independent clusters, not merely from many signers, so a basalt wall of one captured cluster adds nothing once its quota is spent. An attacker who plants a clone behind a cedar screen of rented validators still needs a second, unrelated cluster to agree, and that second cluster has no reason to trust hardware it has never seen operate. Climbing a fresh ridge of cross-cluster consensus for every extra identity costs real infiltration time in a new community, a price that multiplies with each clone and cannot be paid once and copied.
